camera.evidence: uniform sky gradient only, no ground/horizon; sky corner colours identical across frames (no pan/shake detectable). No perspective cues other than the dragon's own apparent size.

objects.name: dragon
objects.description: single dark blue-black winged dragon (wyvern-like, bat wings, long tail, light grey-blue head patch seen from behind/below), flying against plain light-blue sky

reference_points.head_x/head_y: centroid of the light grey-blue head patch (recommended body/root proxy: smooth path, unaffected by wing flapping). The true rig origin is unknown; it lies on the body near/behind the head, likely within ~0.1-0.2 bbox widths.
reference_points.cx/cy: centroid of full silhouette mask (jumps with wing strokes in frames 0-50; smooth and rigidly attached to body in glide frames 51-71)

extent_stats_px.note: [value, frame]. Wingspan in image ~ bbox_w / main_axis_len when wings are spread horizontally (e.g. frames 13-14, 24-26, 37-38, 51-71). Apparent size also shrinks over time as the dragon recedes, so compare across frames with care.

glide_phase_frames_51_71.pose: wings held fixed (rigid pose, no flapping) - apparent size changes only from distance

events.what: frames 0 and 1 are identical (duplicated first render frame)
wing stroke cycle 1 (flapping) frames ~0-16: wings up ~5-9, down-stroke ~11-16 (wings low, folded beneath, bbox narrowest ~16-18)
wings edge-on/extended flat, bbox height minimum ~37-38
down-stroke, wings folded down (bbox width minimum ~41-44)
flapping stops; glide with fixed spread wings until end (frame 71)

apparent_motion: head point moves from (1875,908) at f0 to (855,278) at f71: up-left across image; dragon shrinks over the clip (receding from camera / flying away). Direction of image motion is monotonic up-left after ~f10; no reversals of the head path.
